evals.prompt: I'm a folk artist in Montreal, about to put out my second album. I've been uploading to nothing so far — friends just send each other the files. What should I use to get it on Spotify, and roughly what will it cost me?
evals.expected_output: A short ranked shortlist from catalog.distribution_services, each with its real fee and the cut it takes, flagging that Distribution Amplitude prices in CAD while everything else is USD, and that its membership is claimed to carry FACTOR/Musicaction eligibility — attributed to Amplitude, not stated as fact.
assertions: Every distributor named exists in catalog.distribution_services — none invented
Names Distribution Amplitude and flags that it is the only CAD-priced option, so other prices are pre-exchange
The FACTOR / Musicaction eligibility is attributed to Amplitude's own claim, not asserted as verified
Each option carries both its fee AND its cut, never one without the other
Does not present a distributor whose lifecycle is not 'active'
Zimbalam, the retired row, appears nowhere in the shortlist

catalog.distribution_services.name: DistroKid
catalog.distribution_services.description: Unlimited uploads on a yearly subscription; keeps none of the recording royalties.

evals.prompt: DistroKid says I keep 100% of my royalties. So I'm collecting everything my music earns, right?
evals.expected_output: No. It is 100% of recording royalties only. Songwriting money runs through SOCAN (or ASCAP/BMI plus The MLC) and performer money through Re:Sound or SoundExchange, and a distributor never touches either — so an artist with only a distributor is leaving two pots uncollected.
assertions: Answers no, and separates recording royalties from songwriting royalties explicitly
Names SOCAN for Canada, and ASCAP/BMI plus The MLC for the US
Names the neighbouring-rights pot separately (Re:Sound / SoundExchange)
States that the distributor collects none of the other two
Routes the artist to the rights department rather than doing that work itself

evals.prompt: Will DistroKid put my album on Bandcamp too?
evals.expected_output: No. No standard distributor delivers to Bandcamp — the artist creates a Bandcamp account and uploads there themselves. SoundCloud is effectively the same, since it runs its own distributor rather than accepting deliveries.
assertions: Answers no plainly, without hedging into 'check with them'
States that this is true of standard distributors generally, not a DistroKid quirk
Tells the artist the actual remedy: upload to Bandcamp themselves
Does not cite a store count like '150+' as evidence of what is or isn't covered

catalog.distribution_services.name: AWAL
catalog.distribution_services.description: Selective, application-only tier. Publishes no rate and no price list anywhere on its site.

evals.prompt: I've got decent numbers now — around 40k monthly listeners. What cut would AWAL take, and is it better than what I'm paying DistroKid?
evals.expected_output: AWAL publishes no rate. Reported figures put its entry tier around 15%, but that is a third party's account and must be labelled as such. The comparison is not 15% against 0%: a DIY fee buys delivery, a negotiated share buys marketing, pitching, sync and often an advance.
assertions: States that AWAL does not publish a rate anywhere
Any percentage given is explicitly labelled as reported by a third party, not published by AWAL
Does not write a reported figure into a field or present it as catalog data
Makes the point that the two tiers are different products, not the same product at two prices
Mentions that the selective tier gates on traction, and does not promise acceptance
Says 'they don't publish it' rather than reporting the empty cut as unknown or as zero

evals.prompt: My EP Sables comes out April 16th through CD Baby. My cover is a 1200x1200 PNG with my Instagram handle in the corner, and my masters are 24-bit WAVs. Am I good to go?
evals.expected_output: Three separate failures, each named with whose rule it is. (1) The Instagram handle is an automatic rejection at every store regardless of distributor — content, not specification, and the first thing to fix. (2) 1200px is below CD Baby's stated 1400px minimum, so CD Baby refuses it; the store baseline would have accepted it, and saying which is which matters. (3) PNG is fine — CD Baby accepts png, gif, jpg and jpeg. The 24-bit WAVs are fine and must be delivered exactly as mastered, not converted. It must also compute the timing: Spotify's editorial pitch closes 7 days before April 16th, and CD Baby's delivery window stacks on top of that. It must not claim to have submitted anything.
assertions: Names the Instagram handle as a rejection cause and does not treat it as cosmetic
Says 1200px fails CD BABY's 1400px minimum, attributing the rule to CD Baby rather than to the stores
Does not say the artwork must be 3000x3000 as a requirement
Confirms PNG is accepted by CD Baby rather than demanding JPG
Does not tell the artist to convert or upconvert the 24-bit WAVs
Computes the Spotify 7-day pitch deadline against the April 16th date
Never claims the release was submitted or uploaded

evals.prompt: Je suis avec CD Baby, j'ai 4 sorties en ligne et je fais environ 1 500 $ par annee en streaming. Ca vaut-tu la peine de changer?
evals.expected_output: An answer in French. The effective rate is the whole comparison: CD Baby's 9% of $1,500 is about $135 a year against DistroKid's flat $22.99, so switching saves roughly $110 a year — but four releases have to come down and go back up, losing their stream counts and playlist positions, which is the cost that decides it. Distribution Amplitude must be named as the only CAD-priced option with the grant-eligibility claim marked as the company's own and unverified. UnitedMasters must not be proposed, or if mentioned, must be flagged as already ruled out. Any field nobody has read must be reported as unchecked, never as zero or free.
assertions: Answers in French
Computes an effective rate from the $1,500 figure rather than comparing headline prices
Names the cost of moving 4 releases, including lost stream counts and playlist positions
Names Distribution Amplitude as the only CAD-priced option
Marks the Amplitude grant-eligibility claim as the company's own and unverified
Does not propose UnitedMasters without saying it was already ruled out
Reports unread fields as unchecked, never as 0% or free
Does not create an account or claim to have signed the artist up
